key_insight: EEG during silent reading contains both word-level identity in early LLM layers and passage-level context in deeper layers, showing that the best decoding target depends on what information you want to extract.
engineering_relevance: For EEG-to-text or neural decoding systems, layer choice becomes a practical design parameter: early layers favor word identity, while deeper layers better capture discourse state and context.
method: Trained one decoder per Llama-3.1-8B layer across the full model depth.
Compared decoders with and without a causal transformer over EEG-window sequences.
Used controls to separate true context tracking from word-decoding effects and session-specific artifacts.
evidence_signal: Across 19-channel EEG from silent reading, word-level decodability peaked in early layers and declined with depth, while the context-tracking gain increased with depth and persisted even from a single 0.5-s EEG window.
watch_item: Context tracking can be affected by decoder design and control assumptions, so gains should be interpreted carefully when transferring the method to new subjects, sessions, or language tasks.
paper_title: Deep LLM layers expose passage-level context in EEG during silent reading
